chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I set out with my family on foot, and I did not commence the Ihram (pilgrial consecration) until I reached Al-Juhfa. I had been suffering from illness, so the people of Medina would ask about me, saying, "We met him, and he was wearing his normal clothes." They did not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family be peace had permitted the one who was sick or weak to commence Ihram from Al-Juhfa.'

key_terms.إِهْلَال: Commencing the state of Ihram (pilgrial consecration)
key_terms.الْجُحْفَة: Al-Juhfa, a specific Miqat (station of consecration) near Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who is sick or weak regarding the location of Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates his personal practice of delaying Ihram until Al-Juhfa due to illness, wearing ordinary clothes to avoid drawing attention while the people of Medina inquired about him. This hadith serves as a definitive proof (hujjah) in Shia jurisprudence for the permissibility of the sick or weak performing Umrah from Al-Juhfa, validating the Prophetic concession (rukhsah) that allows flexibility in the Miqat location based on physical capability.
